summary: Resolved for current direct-provider compile scope. Antigravity CLI, direct Cursor Agent OAuth/session, native Cursor API-key/SDK, Claude Code first-party `claude.ai`, and OpenCode server `opencode/big-pickle` were verified in their own lanes. Gemini CLI is removed/retired. GitHub Copilot direct hosted API is green through `https://api.githubcopilot.com` with verified `/models` and `/chat/completions`; because PM is not bridging `copilot` or `gh copilot`, no-env stored CLI credential failures are optional/future-route evidence only and must not block direct-provider implementation readiness. OpenCode-server-routed GitHub Copilot and `opencode-cursor` are not closure evidence for this PM-baked direct-provider retest.

Resolved for the native Cursor direct-provider/API-key route. Jared supplied a Cursor API key for live testing and said not to put it in the ledger; the key is not recorded in ledger files. Direct `@cursor/sdk` model discovery returned 31 live models and prompt execution returned exactly `cursor-api-sdk-ok`. The composer-api standalone Responses proxy verified `/v1/models`, non-streaming Responses, response retrieval, streaming Responses SSE, and image input with a red PNG returning `red`. The local-agent bridge verified non-streaming text, streaming NDJSON, and client-tool forwarding via SDK `mcp` to `providerIdentifier: client`. The temp Worker `/v1` route verified models, chat completions, chat streaming, Responses create/retrieve, and chat tool calls after local external-bridge config. Repo tests and typecheck passed. Remaining caveats are not blockers for native Cursor planning: the signed production macOS app itself was not installed, Worker external-bridge image bytes are not verified, and Worker Responses lacks `output_text`; these are captured as compatibility caveats. `opencode-cursor` remains non-primary/source-lineage because PM has native support and OpenCode requires the plugin for Cursor.

Resolved by explicit planning disposition, not by blanket green support. Kimi For Coding remains green for tested text/thinking/image-input and blocked/unsupported for native image creation. MiniMax global remains green for tested text/thinking/image-input plus `image-01` image creation; MiniMax Image-01 is implementation-shaped from official OpenAPI and local base64 proof, while MiniMax CN remains a separate credential/profile route. Z.AI/Zhipu remains green for tested `glm-4.5-air`, `glm-4.7`, `glm-5-turbo`, alternate Zhipu base, and `glm-5-turbo` reasoning_effort; remaining Z.AI states (`glm-5.1`/`glm-5.2` temporary overload, `glm-5v-turbo` plan-not-included, and image-generation balance/resource gating) are accepted as upstream/account states to compile as disabled/capability-gated rows where not green. Jared clarified he is not buying additional subscription plans now, so Alibaba/Qwen, Tencent, KUAE, Umans, MiniMax CN, and other unpurchased or unverified coding-plan families must not remain purchase blockers; if retained in scope, they require disabled/unverified/capability-gated rows until direct E2E proof exists. Current OpenCode/Models.dev config for all coding-plan provider IDs is recorded as source-lineage for PM-owned provider/model mapping, not as closure evidence.
